receipts.receiptSource: Original Receipt in the 15th Century 'Austin Manuscripts' (Austin 1440)
receipts.receiptText: Swan rosted. Cut a Swan in the rove [roof] of the mouthe toward the brayne enlonge, and let him blede, and kepe the blode for chawdewyn; or elles knytte a knot on his nek, And so late his nekke breke; then skald him. Drawe him and roast him even as thou doest goce in a poyntes, and serve him fort wit chawd-wine.

receipts.receiptSource: Original Receipt in the verse cookery book 'Liber Cure Cocorum', 1430 (Liber Cure 1430);
receipts.receiptText:
Sawce for swannus.
Take tho offal and tho lyver of tho swan,
In gode brothe thou sethe hom than;
When hit is sothyne, take oute the bonus,
Smalle hew tho flesshe, Syr, for the nonus;
Make alyoure of crust of brede,
Of blode of swanne, that sothun is lede,
Caste powdur of gynger and clawes ther to,
Of peper and wyn thou take also,
And salt hit then and sethe hit wele;
Cast in thy flesshe, hewen yche a dele,
And messe hit forthe, as I the kenne,
Set hit in sale before goode menne
